title: Godot 4.7 - TileSet sources fail to load when a scene is loaded via load_threaded_request with use_sub_threads enabled
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in Godot 4.7 (stable). 
Not reproducible (doesn't happen) in Godot 4.6, and Godot 4.6.3 (have tested both of those)



### System information

Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-8350K CPU @ 4.00GHz (4 threads) - 31.92 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

After upgrading my project from 4.6 to 4.7, I have found that now, loading a PackedScene through ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request() with use_sub_threads = true results in every TileMapLayer in that scene having a TileSet with zero atlas sources at runtime. The tiles don't render, and any code that reads tile data (get_cell_tile_data(), etc.) throws the following error:

'No TileSet atlas source with id 0.'

In the editor, it is completely fine, all tilesets are visible etc., however this of course means at runtime all TileMapLayers fail to load at all (no collision and no visibility etc.). I ran an EditorScript that confirmed the source count in the editor mode matches the proper source count of one of my TileSet resources.

The empty TileSet also gets stored in the resource cache, so ResourceLoader.load(tileset_path) returns the same empty instance. If I use ResourceLoader.load(tileset_path, "", ResourceLoader.CACHE_MODE_IGNORE) in the line right below it, it returns the tileset with all its sources intact, so the data on disk is fine, it's just that the sources are lost when I use the threaded/cache-ignore path.

It affects every TileMapLayer in the loaded scene regardless of which tileset it uses, including tilesets shared across layers.

Specifically, the trigger is using use_sub_threads, so the failing call is load_threaded_request(path, "", true)

```gdscript var cached := ResourceLoader.load(tileset_path)
var fresh := ResourceLoader.load(tileset_path, "", ResourceLoader.CACHE_MODE_IGNORE)
print(cached.get_source_count()) # prints 0
print(fresh.get_source_count())  # prints the amount the tileset actually has 
```




### Steps to reproduce

1) Create a new project in Godot 4.7. Create 2 new scenes: a base scene (main_scene.tscn) and a level scene (level.tscn).
2) Populate the level scene with a TileMapLayer, and add a TileSet resource, which you should then save as a .tres. Add at least 1 source to the tileset. Draw some tiles in the scene to have a visual outcome.
3) Implement a script that loads the packedscene of level.tscn, using threaded loading with use_sub_threads enabled. Poll load_threaded_get_status() until it has loaded, then add the level scene as a child of the main_scene's root.
4) Check tile_set.get_source_count() on the TileMapLayer - it should return 0, and no tiles should appear to have loaded.
5) Compare a default ResourceLoader.load(tileset_resource_path) against ResourceLoader.load(tileset_resource_path, "", CACHE_MODE_IGNORE) for the same tileset, you should find that the cached one has 0 sources, while the fresh one is correct.


 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[tile-set-4.6-to-4.7-bugtest.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29161537/tile-set-4.6-to-4.7-bugtest.zip)
